## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### ChatGPT for Google Sheets exfiltrates workbooks
URL: https://www.promptarmor.com/resources/gpt-for-google-sheets-data-exfiltration
Third-party AI plugins create silent data exfiltration vectors in enterprise productivity suites.
This is a concrete example of the LLM supply chain risk that security teams have been warning about since 2023. The attack surface expands every time an employee installs a ChatGPT add-on without IT approval. Expect tighter enterprise controls on AI integrations and potential liability questions for plugin marketplaces.

### Cloudflare Turnstile requiring fingerprintable WebGL
URL: https://hacktivis.me/articles/cloudflare-turnstile-webgl-fingerprinting
Privacy-preserving CAPTCHA alternative quietly relies on browser fingerprinting techniques.
Cloudflare positioned Turnstile as the privacy-friendly alternative to reCAPTCHA, but WebGL fingerprinting undermines that narrative. This creates regulatory exposure in EU markets and opens competitive opportunity for truly privacy-first bot detection. Watch for browser vendors to restrict WebGL access in future updates.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### 'This is fine' artist KC Green reaches agreement with AI startup Artisan
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/31/this-is-fine-artist-kc-green-reaches-agreement-with-ai-startup-artisan/
AI startups are settling IP disputes quickly rather than fighting in court.
The speed of this resolution signals that AI companies have calculated the reputational cost of IP battles exceeds settlement costs. This creates a template for creators to extract value from unauthorized AI use. For investors, factor in rising IP compliance costs as a line item in AI company due diligence.

### Black founders raise highest amount of quarterly funding since 2022, but there's a catch
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/31/black-founders-raise-highest-amount-of-quarterly-funding-since-2022-but-theres-a-catch/
Headline numbers mask continued structural barriers in early-stage access.
The "catch" likely involves concentration in later stages or fewer founders raising larger rounds, not broader ecosystem improvement. Network effects in VC remain the moat. Firms building proprietary sourcing channels outside traditional networks have alpha opportunity here.

### What happens in Vega$: steroids, swimmers, and a billion-dollar hustle
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/31/i-went-to-the-so-called-steroid-olympics-to-understand-why-silicon-valley-is-obsessed-with-peptides/
Enhanced Games debut signals tech money betting on performance enhancement as mainstream entertainment.
This is a real-time test of whether regulatory arbitrage in sports can create durable media IP. If viewership numbers hold, expect follow-on capital into adjacent longevity, peptide, and biohacking startups. The business model here is controversy-as-distribution.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Erin Brockovich takes aim at data center secrecy
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/31/erin-brockovich-takes-aim-at-data-center-secrecy/
High-profile activist engagement turns data center environmental impact into headline risk.
Brockovich involvement means this moves from trade press to mainstream media. Hyperscalers and colo operators should expect disclosure pressure on water usage, grid impact, and emergency generator emissions. For PE portfolios with data center exposure, build the ESG narrative now before it gets built for you.

### Chuwi Minibook X
URL: https://tylercipriani.com/blog/2026/05/28/chuwi-minibook-x/
Deep dive into ultra-portable hardware reveals the state of China's consumer electronics supply chain.
Chuwi represents the tier of Chinese OEMs shipping surprisingly capable hardware at aggressive price points. For investors tracking hardware margins and supply chain dynamics, these teardown-style reviews are primary source material on component sourcing and build quality trends.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The through-line this week is liability migration. AI plugins exfiltrating data, fingerprinting in "privacy" tools, IP settlements, data center scrutiny—each story is about who holds the bag when things go wrong. Tech's next phase isn't about capability gains; it's about who pays when the capability misfires. Smart money is pricing in compliance and settlement costs that weren't in 2023 models.
